content.thinking:
I'm planning to use a sweep for the head too, defining a short path with a radius function so it tapers naturally, and using flat-faced (non-smooth) segments with around 8 sides to create a faceted, low-poly look across the rings.

Now I'm sketching out the skin paint function: a Worley cell pattern generates crack lines along cell edges, a base tone mixes dark and light skin colors with per-cell variation, and dust accumulates near the ground and on upward-facing surfaces while the underside stays darker. I'm also considering adding ring-based creases along limbs and trunk using a periodic fold pattern layered on top of the cell texture, while keeping an eye on paint evaluation cost per texel.

I'm weighing texture resolution against performance, likely settling on 2048 unless it's too slow. For the ears, I'm planning a pink inner surface with a darker rim, branching veins defined by thin ridges in a noise field, and a dusty freckled patch near the lower edge.

For the eyes, I'm building a dark brown sphere as the eyeball with a tiny amber iris disc and small white highlight sphere, then wrapping an eyelid ridge around it with a fan of lash spikes along the upper arc.

Now I'm adding a brow ridge as a thick low skin tube above the eye and a lower eyelid wrinkle, plus a temporal gland tear-stain painted onto the head texture using distance from a vertical line near the eye to darken a thin streak of skin running down toward the cheek.

For the trunk, I'm layering ring markings based on position along its length using the trunk path, darkening thin bands at a regular period with slight wobble, while the underside gets a lighter pink-grey tone with transverse ridges and the tip takes on a softer pink. For the tusks, I'm giving the ivory base a subtle directional grain with streaks running along the tusk length, darkening toward a worn brownish-yellow tip using a gradient tied to position along the tusk.

Now I'm working out toenail shapes and placement, using small flattened box geometries oriented outward from the foot center with darker rim coloring and fine noise texture for a slightly cracked, aged look.

For the hair, I'm planning svg-based tuft cards for the head crown, tail, and chin, using dark strand strokes scattered across surface hits filtered by normal direction and position, plus sparser bristle scatters along the back and tail root for texture.

I'm also sketching the tail as a chained path of five points parented to the nearest pelvis joint so it follows the rear body motion, with the tuft rendered as a ring of spikes at the tip, and placing the tail root near the rump surface where the body's rear cap ends.

Now I'm working out the rump's cap radius and dome extension, since round caps add extra length beyond the stated path endpoint. I'm adjusting the rear path points to keep the body from extending too far back, tentatively setting the rear surface around z=-2.2 and recalculating the chest-front endpoint to match the overall torso proportions.

Recalculating the centerline heights and radii so the rump doesn't peak too high—adjusting P0 down to 2.3 with smaller ry so the top lands around 3.1, then setting shoulder and belly points accordingly along the path.

I'm defining the radius profile across the body's length, widening at the belly and tapering toward the neck, plus a slight downward sag at midpoint for belly droop. Then I'm checking whether the chest dome near the cap pokes out past where the head mesh should cover it, comparing head top height against chest top height to confirm it's hidden.

Now I'm working out the neck chain structure, parenting it off the last spine joint and sketching coordinates for a couple of neck joints leading up to the head joint.

Setting the head joint position and working out the head sweep path with varying radius functions for forehead width and height, adjusting the vertical placement so the forehead doesn't end up too tall relative to the shoulder height.

Now I'm placing the forehead dome as a bumpy twin-lobe shape with two small spheres, adding flattened cheek ellipsoids on either side, and working out the ear attachment geometry—figuring out where the ear joins the head and sizing the outline so the ear spans roughly 1.85 units tall to match an elephant's proportions.

I'm scaling the ears down slightly (0.9) while keeping them appropriately large for an African elephant look, positioning the bottom edge just above floor level, and angling the ear outward and back about 22 degrees so the flared spread reaches a realistic width with the front edge sitting near the shoulders.

For the ear root, I'm sweeping a thick tube along the attach edge from top to bottom with radius 0.09 to anchor the ear naturally to the head, mirroring the shape for the opposite side since both faces get painted regardless of orientation. Now I'm placing the eyes relative to the head's sweep profile.

I'm figuring out the eye placement by casting a ray from outside the head toward the center to find the surface hit point, then embedding a small sphere (radius 0.05) slightly forward on the face. Since the style is low-poly, I'm using flat shading with fewer segments and disabling smoothing on the sweeps.

Now I'm working on the lower jaw—positioning its joint near the head base, aimed forward and slightly down, then building it as a tapered capsule shape (skin over a jaw bone) that narrows from wider at the hinge to thinner toward the tip.

I'm also adding a pink lower lip patch at the front and a darker pink mouth-interior box tucked under the trunk root. I'm checking whether the head's sweep geometry at the chin area occludes the jaw, adjusting the jaw's vertical center and radius so it protrudes visibly below the head for a believable lip line, then starting the trunk as a separate chain parented to the head, beginning its path right at the trunk root point on the face.

Continuing the trunk points down and forward...

I'm adjusting the tip curve to point upward with a final segment toward (0,0.42,3.7), keeping seven joint names and checking the minimum y stays above ground. For the trunk tip itself, I'm planning a small finger-like cone and lip bump in pink-grey, plus two flattened dark nostril discs facing forward. Now I'm thinking about where the tusks should sprout from on the head.

I'm checking clearance between the tusk and trunk geometry, then adding a darker stained band near the tusk tip and a sheath ring at its base. Now I'm sketching an SVG hair tuft shape for the fur cards.

For surface detail I'm planning thin dark crease loops around the neck, knees, and ankles using the sweep/loop system, sized small so they sit flush against the body rather than sticking out.

Writing bands helper function...

Now thinking about adding fold ridges for extra geometry on legs, neck, and trunk base. For outline notches, smoothing might throw errors if a cut corner crosses another edge, so I'll avoid smoothing and go with smoothing 0 instead — crisp polygon edges that give a clean low-poly look.

Adding toenail color, temporal gland details as small dark discs with stain streaks, and deciding to skip scars, navel, and genitals for simplicity while letting paint handle mud splashes and other surface marks.

Now I'm working out paint logic per limb: legs get horizontal ring creases along the vertical axis, while the trunk and neck use different axis mappings since they curve differently. I'm also deciding foot pad colors and a paler cuticle ring near the top of the foot, then starting to write a helper function for ellipsoid bumps.

I'm figuring out where to attach these bumps — using explicit bone references near spine joints for rigidity rather than relying on nearest-joint defaults, and confirming the joint naming convention (spine1 through spine4, pelvis1) so I can parent the front legs correctly to the right spine segment near the hip area.

Continuing the spine, I'm setting up the neck chain parented to the last spine joint, with two neck segments leading up toward the head, then attaching the head joint to the end of the neck using its chain frame for position and orientation.

Next I'm adding a jaw joint aimed outward from the head, hinge-style ear joints mirrored left and right, and starting a tail chain rooted near the rear of the body, calculating the rear tip position from the body's cap geometry.

Casting a surface ray near the rump to find the tail's root point, then sketching a shortened path of control points tapering down to about waist height so the tail reads closer to real proportions (roughly 1–1.3m) rather than too long.

For the tuft at the tip, I'm placing a ring of short spikes around the final chain point, with each spike oriented outward from the tail but tilted steeply toward the downward tangent direction so they hang naturally rather than sticking straight out.

Moving to the head: I need forehead bumps, cheeks, brow, and eyes, using surface raycasts against a skin sweep to find placement points and normals for each feature, then attaching lashes as a ring around the eye frame. I'm working out the brow geometry as a sweep along a curved spline connecting a few control points above the eye socket.

Still shaping the eyelid geometry... I'll also plan hair card placement across crown, back, and chin regions with varying density per area.

Now I'm working out foot contact and placement: passing a contact parameter with coordinates to the leg rigging, then sizing a cylinder for the foot so it sits just at floor level without floating or sinking too deep, adjusting the leg-to-ankle radius transition to match up cleanly with the foot geometry.

I'm also laying out nail placement around the front edge of each foot, computing positions using angles spread outward from forward-facing direction and a radius from the foot center, then shaping each nail as a small tilted wedge oriented to point outward.

Front feet get 4 nails, hind feet get 3, matching African elephant anatomy. Now I'm thinking through other body details like shoulder bumps as scaled, positioned spheres along the spine.

Counting roughly 64 flat colors total. Now I'm sketching the skin paint function itself—using cellular noise to blend between dark and light skin tones based on a cell distance metric, giving organic patchy variation across the body.

I'm considering quantizing tone values to get faceted, low-poly color cells, and thinking about crease shading with a darker pink tone. Now I'm starting the ear paint logic, blending two ear colors with noise, adding thin dark vein lines, and weighing whether to add a rim highlight based on normal direction.

Still writing paint logic...

Defining leg chain geometry...

For the path spans, I need 3 names plus 1 tip joint to cover 4 points. I'm setting up ring loops along the surface, a fold helper function, and double-checking for unused TypeScript names that could cause errors. I'm also planning the ear hinge rod and scatter/cards calls for surface detail, making sure types like Hit[] and color arrays line up correctly.

I'm now sketching the ear's outline coordinates to form an Africa-like closed loop shape, checking that the edge from bottom to top closes properly at x=0, and positioning the ear base and hinge rod attachment near the joint height.

I'll keep the ears as rigid flat low-poly plates rather than adding curl detail, skip the dewlap fold, and just dust some darker color on the ear lower edges. I'm double-checking the sweep and joint API usage for bones and directions, then sketching out the cheek part geometry using a small sphere segment.

I'm working out jaw and mouth details — a pinkish lip accent near the jaw front, skipping the separate mouth line sweep, and defining a head skin surface reference for eye placement.

Now I'm planning the toe nails and foot geometry per leg via a reusable foot function, picking a dark brown hair color, and adding tail tuft spikes with cards. After writing the file, I'll run typecheck, preview with bounding box, take a shot, and check for gaps.
